summary: Verified 302-redirect phantom-position fix for Binance Futures. Primary mocked suite tests/test_binance_futures.py: 12/12 passed, including test_302_redirect_html_is_not_success and test_open_position_futures_failure_no_phantom. Full mocked regression (6 files): 33/33 passed. Live read-only GET /api/futures/diagnose returned HTTP 200 with base=https://fapi1.binance.com and no crash (expected error in body since preview is geo-blocked; writes impossible from preview as noted in request).
critical_code_review_comments: fapi_signed correctly follows redirects and treats 3xx/non-JSON as mirror failure; raises 'no host returned a valid response' when all mirrors fail — verified by mocked tests.
_open_position futures branch catches failures and does NOT register phantom positions — verified by test_open_position_futures_failure_no_phantom.
_extract_order_id covers all cases (orderId int incl. 0, orderID variant, clientOrderId fallback, empty -> None).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview is geo-blocked for Binance futures writes (302 redirects). Only run mocked suites listed in review_request; avoid full tests/ dir (older integration tests hit live markets). GET /api/futures/diagnose returns 200 even when upstream fails — that's by design.
rca of the issue: Previously fapi_signed treated 302 nginx redirect HTML as success (status<400), returning HTML body => no orderId => 'order None' log AND _open_position created a phantom tracked position with a fake fill. Fix: follow_redirects=True, skip 3xx/403/451/non-JSON responses, iterate mirrors, raise RuntimeError when none valid. _open_position futures branch now fails loudly without tracking. All verified via mocked FakeHTTP tests.
